title: The sync gate reuses a test run's result for the same selection on the same tree
goal: tests.py keys each run by the hash of its selected test ids, the git tree of the index plus the working tree's tracked changes (git write-tree on a temporary index, never the person's) and the Python version, writes the key with the outcome to _cache/tests/results.json after a passing run, and when run by the sync gate (KB_TESTS_FAST=1) with a key the file holds as passed, prints 'reused: <key> from <UTC time>' and exits 0 without starting pytest, recording a test.run row with mode changed and a reused flag; a failing run writes no key, a dirty untracked test file breaks the key, and tests.py --no-reuse forces the run. One planted failure: an edit to a tracked test file after a passing run changes the key and pytest runs again. After it lands, the digest's sync.gate tests.py-changed mean time falls below half of 2026-W41's.
notes: Premise (ops sidecars, all time to 2026-10-08): sync.gate rows where tests.py-changed ran: 733, mean 77.8 s, about 15.8 hours in all; the same selection on the same tree runs again whenever a landing retries (land.step kbgit.py-sync-push failed 256 times, rebase 231) or several items land from one tip. A reused flag on test.run is a new key of a closed event: ql_capture.OPS_EVENTS and the Surfaces paragraph of kb/_self/querylog.md change in the same commit. The key must be a tree the gate can trust: the index plus tracked working-tree changes, never a path list, so an edit to any tracked file after the run invalidates it; untracked files are what tests.py already refuses to scan (kb/_self/maintaining.md: stage new files first). Filed under EP-hlnsqx4f (the suite runs in minutes) as the gate-side half; ST-akicahgy is the index-side half. Precheck 2026-10-08: both checks pass before the work: the planted failure (an edit to a tracked test file after a passing run changes the key and pytest runs again; a reused run prints reused: and starts no pytest) is added to test_sync_e2e.py by the work, and --ceiling pins the suite size.
